subject: SLA derivation and load synthesis protocol for RFP - measurement plan
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP - request for measurement protocol and thresholds

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our RFP scoring we need a concise and reproducible measurement protocol that we can run (or have partners run) to validate your claims around latency/throughput and scaling behavior. Specifically the procurement and SRE teams want: 
- Clear test harness steps (what to run, warmup, how to seed inputs)
- Reporting format and the metrics you recommend we capture (p50/p95/p99, tail, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, open file descriptors)
- Load synthesis guidance for concurrency mixes (short chat bursts vs long generation), target QPS ranges, and target sequence lengths
- Any model variants (quantized vs fp16) and important config knobs (batch size, KV cache warmup)

Could you provide a single document we can attach to the RFP? Ideally it should include example invocation commands, a sample config, and an expected table of results for the reference model. Would you also note any caveats/assumptions we should treat as part of scoring?

Timeline: procurement needs something by end-of-day Thursday our time (2027-06-03).

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior Sourcing Manager, Globex
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - request for measurement protocol and thresholds

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a compact measurement protocol we use for RFPs (redwood_load_protocol_v1.pdf) and an example test_config.yaml that enumerates common blends. High-level summary below so your team can score quickly: 

Summary points:
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side, excluding client overhead), end-to-end tokens/sec, GPU utilization, 99.9th percentile kernel stalls. Also report request size, response tokens, and cache hit-rate for prefix caching.
- Warmup: 3-minute progressive warmup with 10%/30%/60%/100% load steps to stabilize JIT/compilation and KV cache.
- Concurrency mix: provide two canonical mixes — "interactive chat" (200ms target p95; short 16 token outputs; high QPS) and "long generation" (up to 1024 tokens, relaxed p95 target). The test_config includes QPS bins and concurrency per worker.
- Model variants: include fp16 and int8-quantized variants. Run both with identical workloads; quantify delta in p95 and token/sec.
- Batching: measure three batch targets: 1, 4, 16; report effective latency and throughput per GPU.

Caveats/assumptions:
- Results assume a stable cluster with no autoscaling events during the window. If your test harness triggers autoscale, annotate the timeline.
- For caching tests, prefix KV cache must be preloaded with representative prefixes (we include a script in the doc).

Attachments: redwood_load_protocol_v1.pdf (protocol + example scripts), example_test_config.yaml, summary_latency_matrix.csv (example results).

We can provide a one-hour walkthrough of the protocol if you want us to run a proof-of-concept and share raw logs. If procurement needs the artifacts by EOD Thu 2027-06-03, we'll prioritize a tailored run for Globex.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - request for measurement protocol and thresholds

Looping in a few additional details we should surface in the protocol before final delivery: 

1) Test harness instrumentation 
- Recommend using our open load-generator (link in doc) or k6 for request shaping. Require metric export to Prometheus with labels: model_version, quantization, batch_size, seq_len, client_zone.

2) SLA derivation guidance (important for scoring)
- Provide an SLO derivation table: baseline p95 under nominal load (e.g., 100 concurrent users, median seq_len 64) and headroom multipliers (1.25x, 1.5x, 2x) that map to cluster sizes. This gives procurement a deterministic formula to translate measured p95 into committed capacity.

3) Failure modes and experiment controls
- Include tests for cache-stress (cache cold -> warmup), kernel-saturation (high-batch low-concurrency), and node-failure (kill one GPU mid-run) — report how latency shifts and recovery time.

Marcus — can you add the example SLO table and a mock cluster-size mapping to the CSV? I'll review and then we can finalize.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - request for measurement protocol and thresholds

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple follow-ups from the SRE scoring rubric: 

- Can you provide example invocation commands (curl or python) that show streaming vs non-streaming modes and the headers we should capture?
- For reporting: we'd like a csv template with these columns: timestamp, request_id, model_version, quantization, batch_size, seq_len, latency_ms, status_code, gpu_util_percent, mem_mb, cache_hit. The example_summary csv you sent is helpful but please align to this schema.
- Are you comfortable including an annotated example run (one hour) where Redwood runs the harness in our account and drops the raw Prometheus and trace exports into a shared Drive? That would greatly speed procurement sign-off.

We also need to confirm the delivery timeline by EOD Thu (your time). If Redwood can run the demo in our account, please indicate prerequisites (service account, IP allowlist, duration).

Regards,
Samantha
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - request for measurement protocol and thresholds

Samantha —

We can deliver the annotated run and aligned CSV by EOD Thu 2027-06-03. Action items below: 

1) Deliverables (by EOD Thu):
- redwood_load_protocol_v1.pdf (finalized with instrumentation commands)
- example_test_config.yaml (canonical blends: interactive, mixed, long-gen)
- summary_latency_matrix.csv (SLO derivation and cluster-size mapping, aligned to your CSV schema)
- one-hour annotated run (we will push Prometheus and trace exports to the shared Drive link you provide)

2) Prereqs for running in your account:
- Temporary service account with read/write to a dedicated GCS bucket or Drive folder (we'll upload logs there).
- IP allowlist for 13.52.45.11/32 (Redwood test runner), or an SSH bastion (we can adapt).
- Test window: 1 hour during low-production traffic (we recommend UTC 02:00-04:00).

3) Example invocation snippets (included in the protocol):
- Non-streaming: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":64}'
- Streaming (python sample included): python examples/stream_client.py --model rwd-7b --seq-len 64

We'll update the CSV to match your columns and share the Drive link once uploads are complete. Alex/Evelyn — I'll attach the final CSV and protocol to this thread once I finish a quick pass.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Performance Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
